title: External Dataset Expansion and Validation Audit

issue_1_noise_floor_interpretation.finding: Conflation of true sensor noise floor with multi-appliance switching volatility.
issue_1_noise_floor_interpretation.defect_critique: In Milestone 2C.7, 112.66 W was referred to as the 'empirical mains noise' or 'sensor noise floor'. This is scientifically inaccurate. The true sensor metrology noise of the Schneider EM6400 is Class 1.0 (< 1-2 W). The 112.66 W figure is the overall standard deviation of first differences across all domestic activities, which is dominated by major appliance on/off transitions (ACs cycling 1500-2500 W, washing machine drum agitation, compressor start-up surges). During 97.0% of the monitoring period when no major appliance is switching (|delta_P| < 50 W), the background baseline standard deviation is actually 8.09 W (IQR 4.21 W), and during quiet steady-state (|delta_P| < 10 W) it is 3.41 W.
issue_1_noise_floor_interpretation.correction: Separate terminology: (1) Metrology Sensor Noise Floor (sigma ~ 1-2 W), (2) Quiescent Domestic Baseline Jitter (sigma ~ 8.09 W, IQR ~ 4.21 W), and (3) Multi-Appliance Switching Volatility (gross sigma ~ 112.66 W). SNR for a 12 W load must be evaluated against quiescent jitter (SNR ~ 12 / 8.09 = 1.48) and distractor overlap rather than gross switching variance.

issue_2_voltage_sensitivity.finding: Theoretical ohmic assumption (P proportional to V^2) overstates real residential power sensitivity by an order of magnitude.
issue_2_voltage_sensitivity.defect_critique: Milestone 2C.7 stated that an ordinary 1 V grid sag on a 1.2 kW load produces an 11.4 W power drop. While mathematically true for a purely linear ohmic resistance (R = const), modern households are composite ZIP loads. Switch-mode power supplies (laptops, TVs, LED drivers, phone chargers) with active power factor correction act as constant-power loads (P = const, dP/dV ~ 0). Inverter ACs and induction motors also weakly regulate shaft power. Regression on genuine quiescent iAWE telemetry reveals an empirical slope of only 0.47 W/V on Phase 1 (~1.0 W/V whole house), roughly 10x lower than the purely resistive model.
issue_2_voltage_sensitivity.correction: Document that real homes exhibit composite ZIP load behavior with weak voltage correlation (r = 0.0701). A 1 V voltage sag produces ~1.0 W of whole-house baseline shift, not 11.4 W. However, large utility voltage drops of 10-20 V (frequent in developing grids) still produce 10-20 W baseline shifts that can alias into 12 W loads.

issue_3_persistence_baseline.finding: Persistence baseline operates as an oracle upper bound requiring ground truth y_{t-1} at test time.
issue_3_persistence_baseline.defect_critique: Persistence relies on the ground-truth submeter state at the immediately preceding sample (y_{t-1}). In any practical NILM system, the submeter does not exist at inference time. While Persistence provides a valuable theoretical oracle benchmark reflecting state autocorrelation (appliance run-lengths), it cannot be compared directly against whole-house algorithms as a deployable candidate.
issue_3_persistence_baseline.correction: Formally flag Persistence as ORACLE_BENCHMARK in all machine-readable schemas and reports, and exclude it from the ranked list of deployable models.

issue_4_event_matching_tolerance_bypass.finding: Onset tolerance constraint was bypassed whenever predicted and ground-truth events overlapped in time.

audit_evidence.consequence: An event starting 5 minutes late into a 10-minute ground-truth run was marked as a True Positive onset detection even when tolerance_s = 60s.
audit_evidence.delay_cancellation: Mean delay was computed as np.mean(delays), allowing early detections (-15s) and late detections (+15s) to cancel to 0.0s.

issue_4_event_matching_tolerance_bypass.defect_critique: In evaluate_events.py, the condition 'or has_overlap' allowed any predicted event overlapping an ongoing cycle to be considered a candidate match, regardless of how late it started. In NILM, onset detection evaluates whether the turn-on transition was captured within a specified time window. Allowing late events to match defeated the purpose of tolerance_s.
issue_4_event_matching_tolerance_bypass.correction: Updated evaluate_events.py with require_onset_tolerance=True (default). Candidates must strictly satisfy |onset_diff| <= tolerance_s. Added mean_signed_delay_s, mean_absolute_delay_s, and max_absolute_delay_s to prevent delay cancellation. Added unit tests in test_evaluation_audit.py.

issue_5_temporal_leakage_and_splits.finding: Chronological partitioning strictly verified with 100-sample boundary buffer drops.
issue_5_temporal_leakage_and_splits.audit_notes: Chronological ordering is strictly maintained. The 100-sample buffers (600s) completely isolate the 5-sample (30s) rolling feature lookbacks. Hyperparameters (thresholds, step sizes) were fit strictly on Train and tuned on Val; Test was evaluated strictly once.

issue_6_metric_validity_and_class_imbala.finding: Inactive sample dominance dilutes active regression error by a factor of 2,800.
issue_6_metric_validity_and_class_imbala.audit_notes: Milestone 2C.7 correctly decomposed the overall MAE into active and inactive sub-populations via the mathematical identity MAE_all = w_active * MAE_active + w_inactive * MAE_inactive. The 1.76 W overall score is completely dominated by the 95,236 inactive samples. Reporting active MAE (476.48 W) and RETE (41.93%) is mandatory to prevent misleading claims.

issue_7_data_alignment_and_missing_imput.finding: 10.10% of 6s intervals in the submeter were missing during energized mains periods and silently imputed as 0.0 W.
issue_7_data_alignment_and_missing_imput.defect_critique: During 48,132 six-second intervals (~80.2 hours) where the whole-house mains was energized, the CurrentCost motor submeter failed to record data (due to 433 MHz RF packet drops or sensor sleep). The pipeline filled these missing intervals with 0.0 W (motor OFF). If the motor operated during any of these unobserved intervals, ground-truth activations were missed, and any correct aggregate detection during those windows would have been falsely scored as a False Positive.
issue_7_data_alignment_and_missing_imput.correction: Document the 10.10% RF dropout rate explicitly. In future pipelines, discard unobserved submeter intervals from test evaluation rather than assuming unmetered periods are always 0.0 W.

issue_8_reproducibility.finding: Deterministic seeds, recorded software versions, and pipeline reproducibility verified.

iawe.name: iAWE (Indian Dataset for Ambient Water and Energy)
iawe.citation: Batra et al., 'It\'s Different: Insights into home energy consumption in India', ACM BuildSys 2013, pp. 1-8.
measurements_submeter: P, Q, S, V, I, f, PF (meters 3-11 jplugs)
iawe.operating_environment: Concurrent living in a 3-floor residential home in Delhi, India
iawe.supports_unique_attribution: Supports high-power motors/ACs; insufficient for 12 W lighting

dinar_sensors_2025.name: High-Frequency Harmonic NILM Dataset (Dinar et al., 2025)
dinar_sensors_2025.citation: Dinar, F.; Paris, S.; Busvelle, É. 'Capturing High-Frequency Harmonic Signatures for NILM: Building a Dataset for Load Disaggregation.' Sensors 2025, 25(15), 4601. DOI: 10.3390/s25154601.
dinar_sensors_2025.file_size: ~250 MB to 1 GB across multiple daily recording sessions (CSV format)
dinar_sensors_2025.sampling_frequency: 8 kHz analog front-end sampling on ATM90E36A; pre-computed harmonic metrics h1-h32 logged at ~1 Hz cadence
dinar_sensors_2025.channels_aggregate: 4 sensor nodes with 3 phases each (12 total physical channels)
dinar_sensors_2025.channels_submeter: Appliance-level plug channels for Hair dryer, Electric water heater, Fridge, Clothes iron, Hair straightener, Laptop charger
dinar_sensors_2025.operating_environment: Controlled and semi-controlled residential test environment
dinar_sensors_2025.supports_unique_attribution: High discriminative power for harmonic non-linear loads (SMPS, rectifiers) via h1-h32; unverified for 12 W LED bulb in mixed aggregate

uk_dale.name: UK-DALE (UK Domestic Appliance-Level Electricity)
uk_dale.citation: Kelly, J., & Knottenbelt, W. 'The UK-DALE dataset, domestic appliance-level electricity demand and whole-house electrical data from five UK homes.' Scientific Data 2, 150007 (2015). DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2015.7.
uk_dale.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By 1.0) / CC BY 4.0
uk_dale.file_size: ~45 GB total (Houses 1-5); House 1 low-freq is ~1.2 GB compressed / ~10 GB uncompressed; House 1 16 kHz audio waveforms is ~35 GB
uk_dale.sampling_frequency: 16 kHz (V and I waveforms, Houses 1 & 2 mains); 1 Hz (P, S, V mains); 6s (Appliance IAM submeters)
uk_dale.channels_aggregate: Whole-house mains (16 kHz raw waveforms + 1 Hz P, S, V)
uk_dale.channels_submeter: Up to 54 individual appliance monitors in House 1 (solar thermal pump, kettle, laptop, fridge, lights, etc.)
uk_dale.operating_environment: Real-world continuous longitudinal multi-appliance domestic operation (House 1 monitored for > 650 days)
uk_dale.supports_unique_attribution: Supports multi-kW and motor loads; single 12 W LED unmetered (only 100 W 10-bulb ceiling array available)

refit.name: REFIT (Cleaned Electrical Load Profiles from 20 UK Homes)
refit.citation: Murray, D., Stankovic, L., & Stankovic, V. 'An electrical load measurements dataset of United Kingdom households from a two-year longitudinal study.' Scientific Data 4, 160122 (2017). DOI: 10.1038/sdata.2016.122.
refit.file_size: ~1.4 GB total (all 20 houses); ~80 MB per house (e.g. CLEAN_House21.csv)
refit.channels_aggregate: 1 whole-house aggregate active power channel per house
refit.channels_submeter: 9 submetered appliance channels per house (kettles, washing machines, pond pumps, fridges, TVs, etc.)
refit.operating_environment: Real-world continuous living in 20 UK homes over 2 years
refit.supports_unique_attribution: Supports 75 W Pond Pump (House 21); NO voltage, NO reactive power, NO waveforms

plaid.name: PLAID (Plug Load Appliance Identification Dataset)
plaid.citation: Gao et al., 'PLAID: a public dataset of high-resolution electrical engine measurements for load disaggregation', ACM BuildSys 2014.
plaid.channels_submeter: Individual appliance plugs across 11 appliance types (including incandescent, CFL, and LED lamps)
plaid.operating_environment: Isolated bench-top laboratory activations (1-2 second individual bursts)
plaid.supports_unique_attribution: Supports isolated appliance signature classification; DOES NOT support whole-house NILM disaggregation

whited.name: WHITED (Worldwide Household Inventory of Duplicate Electro-Domestic Appliances)
whited.citation: Kahl et al., 'WHITED: A Worldwide Household Inventory of Duplicate Electro-Domestic Appliances', IEEE IGARSS 2016.
whited.channels_submeter: Individual appliance start-up transients for 47 appliance types across 6 regions
whited.operating_environment: Isolated laboratory bench activations (5-second start-up windows)
whited.supports_unique_attribution: Controlled start-up transient classification only; CANNOT prove whole-house aggregate attribution

water_heater_140w.iawe_rationale: iAWE contains zero water heater submeters. Water heating was solar, gas, or unmetered.
water_heater_140w.uk_dale_rationale: House 1 has an unmetered/unused 3 kW immersion heater; kettles are 2.5-3 kW rapid boiling elements.
water_heater_140w.refit_rationale: REFIT houses only meter 2.5-3.0 kW kettles. Downscaling a 3 kW kettle to 140 W is unphysical.
water_heater_140w.dinar_2025_rationale: Includes 'Electric water heater', but typical European domestic cylinders are 1500-2000 W, representing a 10x-14x rating mismatch.
water_heater_140w.plaid_rationale: Contains 1 kW-2 kW space heaters in isolated bursts; no 140 W vessel.
water_heater_140w.overall_verdict: NOT_VALIDATED across all genuine aggregate public datasets.

water_pump_75w.target_physics: Inductive fractional AC motor (PF ~ 0.78), intermittent booster operation
water_pump_75w.iawe_rationale: Meter 12 is a 600-750 W overhead tank lift pump. Provides authentic real-world motor telemetry, but cannot validate the 75 W booster pump class.
water_pump_75w.uk_dale_rationale: House 1 Channel 3 is 'solar_thermal_pump' (~43 W). Shares single-phase induction stator physics, but operating head and duty cycle differ.
water_pump_75w.refit_rationale: House 21 Appliance 9 is 'Pond Pump' (~80 W). Matches power rating (75-80 W) and inductive motor physics, but operates continuously rather than in intermittent domestic cycles.
water_pump_75w.dinar_2025_rationale: Dinar et al. dataset does not include a water pump channel.
water_pump_75w.plaid_rationale: PLAID contains no water pump category.
water_pump_75w.overall_verdict: PARTIALLY_VALIDATED on REFIT House 21 (80 W pond pump) and UK-DALE House 1 (43 W solar pump); NOT_VALIDATED for domestic sump booster duty.

ceiling_fan_45w.target_physics: Multi-speed induction motor (PF ~ 0.91), high aerodynamic rotor inertia
ceiling_fan_45w.iawe_rationale: Ceiling fans are hardwired into ceiling conduit junction boxes on shared lighting circuits, unmetered.
ceiling_fan_45w.uk_dale_rationale: UK climate lacks ceiling fans. House 1 Channel 52 is a small 35 W portable desk fan with negligible rotor inertia.
ceiling_fan_45w.refit_rationale: REFIT contains zero ceiling fan submeters.
ceiling_fan_45w.dinar_2025_rationale: Dinar et al. dataset contains no fan channel.
ceiling_fan_45w.plaid_rationale: PLAID contains isolated desk fans, but no aggregate household disaggregation.
ceiling_fan_45w.overall_verdict: NOT_VALIDATED across all genuine aggregate public datasets.

led_bulb_12w.target_physics: Non-linear switch-mode driver, diode bridge, high harmonic distortion (THD_i > 80%)
led_bulb_12w.iawe_rationale: iAWE contains no isolated lighting channels.
led_bulb_12w.uk_dale_rationale: UK-DALE House 1 only submeters a composite array of 10 downlights (~100 W total on Channel 8). Individual 12 W bulb unmetered.
led_bulb_12w.refit_rationale: REFIT domestic lighting is hardwired into the central consumer unit and completely unmetered.
led_bulb_12w.dinar_2025_rationale: Dinar et al. evaluate laptops, irons, water heaters, hair dryers, and fridges; isolated 12 W LED bulb is unrepresented.
led_bulb_12w.plaid_rationale: PLAID contains isolated high-frequency bursts of compact fluorescent and incandescent lamps on laboratory benches; ZERO whole-house aggregate data.
led_bulb_12w.overall_verdict: NOT_VALIDATED on public whole-house datasets; CONTROLLED_ONLY on bench transient datasets.

high_frequency_harmonic_assessment.key_distinction: Isolated signature classification vs. Concurrent aggregate attribution

analysis.controlled_transient_findings: High-frequency bench datasets (PLAID, WHITED) prove that isolated LED drivers exhibit distinctive non-linear current spikes and high THD_i (> 80%). However, these recordings capture a single bulb connected directly to clean mains power on a laboratory test bench.
analysis.aggregate_mains_reality: In a real residential home, whole-house mains current is a simultaneous superposition of dozens of non-linear loads (laptop SMPS, television power supplies, smart plugs, variable-frequency refrigerator compressors). The 3rd and 5th harmonic currents generated by a single 12 W LED bulb are approximately 30-50 mA RMS.
analysis.harmonic_masking_barrier: A modern 65 W laptop charger or 100 W OLED television generates 200-400 mA of 3rd and 5th harmonic currents. Variations in TV screen brightness or laptop CPU load modulate harmonic currents by 50-100 mA, which completely swamps the 30-50 mA signature of a 12 W LED.
analysis.scientific_verdict: Harmonic metrology (e.g. ATM90E36A h1-h32) is a necessary condition for low-power disaggregation, but IT DOES NOT BY ITSELF SOLVE THE 12 W LED ATTRIBUTION PROBLEM amidst concurrent non-linear domestic distractors.
